{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|We are sending all available troops to meet this army of hers. It appears to be assembling at the edge of the swamp. Primitives, my lord&mdash;nothing better. We do not expect much resistance.|Nute Gunray giving his impressions on the Gungan technology level|<ref name="tpm">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>}}
A '''technology level''' (or '''technological development''') was a classification used by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] bureaucrats to identify the level of technology on a [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. They were implemented in the buying and selling of goods and materials.

==Classification==
The six technology levels were:
[[File:Moon_of_Endor_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|100px|Endor]]
*'''Stone'''&mdash;Such civilizations were distinguished by small social groups, primitive methods of cultivation and the use of simple tools. There was very little need for trade in stone-level cultures, as the tools could usually be made by anyone in the society. Food was provided through gathering wild [[Plant/Legends|plants]] (in case of herbivory), through fishing and hunting (if carnivore) or through early agriculture. Transportation was generally by foot, without any organized road network. Communication was essentially ensured by pictures and storytelling.<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> (e.g. [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], which the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] and the [[Yuzzum/Legends|Yuzzum]] called home)<ref name="GG6">''[[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters]]''</ref>

[[File:Gamorr_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|100px|Gamorr]]
*'''Feudal'''&mdash;Feudal-level civilizations were characterized by extensive social contact at a regional level and simple manufactured goods. The most advanced tools were made by specialized factories or workers. Agriculture, which consisted of herding bred animals or farming planted crops, occupied most of the community. Transportation was ensured by harnessing animal, [[Water/Legends|water]] or wind power; road networks do exist. Communication included the use of a [[Writing/Legends|writing system]].<ref name="AE" /> (e.g. [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]], the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]])<ref name="GG6" />

[[File:Ryloth.jpg|thumb|100px|Ryloth]]
*'''Industrial'''&mdash;In industrial-level civilizations, the population was split between manufacturing and agriculture, as society interacted on a continental basis. The most advanced tools were created through mass production. Electricity was produced from burning fuels. Cultivation and transportation were motorized, and communication included the mass production of written text and simple electrical messages.<ref name="AE" /> (e.g. [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], principal world of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]])<ref name="GG6" />

*'''Atomic'''&mdash;Within atomic-level civilizations, more efficient mass production and manufactured goods were available on almost all societal levels. Advanced plastics and metallic alloys were created. Space travel was being invented while transportation, medicine, communication, and business were growing.<ref name="AE" />

[[File:KubindiNEGAS.jpg|thumb|100px|Kubindi]]
*'''Information'''&mdash;Sophisticated devices of communication and dataprocessing characterized civilizations of the information age. Such cultures had a global community, marked by quick dispersal of information to all inhabited planetary areas. Early [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and energy weapons often appeared, and [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] was close to being discovered. Information-age worlds did not know the secrets of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], but in-[[Star system/Legends|system]] [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel was relatively common sight.<ref name="AE" /> (e.g. [[Kubindi/Legends|Kubindi]], the [[Kubaz/Legends|Kubaz]] homeworld)<ref name="GG6" />

[[File:Dac-AORCR.png|thumb|100px|Dac]]
*'''Space'''&mdash;These civilizations were marked by hyperspace travel, extra-system colonization, droids, personal energy weapons such as [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], and efficient industry.<ref name="AE" /> The space age was genereally considered to be the final stage of development of any civilization.(e.g. [[Dac/Legends|Dac]], the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] and [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] home planet)<ref name="GG6" />

==Cultural prejudices==
{{Quote|The Ewok civilization is extremely primitive and simple, with little of unique interest to warrant study by already overworked Imperial anthropologists.|[[Pfilbee Jhorn]]|<ref name="ISWU" />}}
Societies that were thought to lack technological, economic or cultural development&mdash;like the furry [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]]&mdash;were sometimes described as "primitive". The term, however, often had a [[Speciesism|speciesist]] and discriminatory connotation, and was considered to be offensive.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref><ref name="ISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> Before the fateful events of the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Naboo (people)/Legends|inhabitants]] of the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] thought of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]]&mdash;a race of sentient amphibians with whom they shared their world&mdash;as barbarians.<ref name="E1J:QA">''[[Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala]]''</ref> The role of Gungans in the [[galactic community]] was purposedly downplayed by the [[Naboo Senatorial Delegation]], the members of which described those non-Humans as "simple-minded barbarians who have barely mastered the basic hallmarks of civilization."<ref name="SON">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In the [[2001]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', there are four technology levels, referred to as "tech levels." The player can acquire resources to upgrade their technology level, and each increase gives access to a wider range of buildings, units, and research to utilize.<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>
